title: Theoretical Bounds on Differential-Linear Bias
summary: No theoretical lower or upper bounds are currently available for differential-linear distinguisher bias in the studied setting; establishing such bounds remains open.

formal_statement.body: For differential-linear distinguishers targeting SPN symmetric-key primitives modeled as Markov ciphers, establish theoretically justified lower or upper bounds on the distinguisher bias; currently, no such theoretical bounds are available in this setting.

scope.domain: Differential-linear cryptanalysis of SPN symmetric-key primitives.
assumptions: Target ciphers satisfy the Markov-cipher model.
parameters: Distinguisher bias — the target quantity for theoretical lower or upper bounds
scope.unresolved_remainder: Establish theoretically justified lower or upper bounds on differential-linear distinguisher bias in this setting.

citations.label: New Approaches for Estimating the Bias of Differential-Linear Distinguishers

progress.summary: The paper reports bias estimates for concrete reduced-round distinguishers, then explicitly remarks that it cannot provide theoretical lower or upper bounds. Establishing such bounds remains open in its SPN Markov-cipher setting.
citation_labels: Ting Peng et al., New Approaches for Estimating the Bias of Differential-Linear Distinguishers
